headline: Linux 7.3 improves VRAM stability under heavy load
lede: New kernel heuristics prevent memory-eviction deadlocks when GPUs exceed physical capacity. Systems now handle memory pressure with prioritized swapping instead of crashing.

headline: Bringing functional type safety to database queries
lede: Acadia bridges the gap between high-level language constructs and SQL performance. By treating schema safety as a core guarantee, developers can finally discard error-prone manual migrations.
pullquote: Treating query safety as a core language guarantee resolves the friction between client and database layers.

headline: How Bluesky hides logos in your screenshots
lede: The app exploits iOS field-masking behaviors intended to hide passwords, revealing a secondary layer during system screenshots. It is a quiet, clever subversion of platform privacy features for brand awareness.

headline: OpenRouter slashes GPT-5.6 Sol model costs
lede: The price of flagship reasoning models has dropped significantly as access becomes commoditized. Developers can now integrate complex agentic workflows into production at half the previous cost.

headline: Google buys airline data assets to fuel AI
lede: Google's purchase of a defunct airline's proprietary archives at auction signals a new phase in the data wars. Corporate histories are no longer just records; they are raw training material.

headline: The failed experiment of 1996 Quake shareware
lede: Id Software once attempted to distribute games with locked CD content accessible only via phone-in serial keys. The initiative collapsed quickly when hackers exposed the weak underlying encryption.

headline: Mathematically ranking the world's most brilliant birds
lede: Subjective avian beauty is translated into rigorous, tunable functions using CIE color space data. This method avoids homogeneity by applying maximal marginal relevance to ensure statistical diversity in the final rankings.

headline: Mainline Linux camera drivers arrive for Fairphone 6
lede: A successful driver porting project brings functional main-camera support to postmarketOS users. The effort aims to establish a non-profit model for sustainable, ethical hardware development.

headline: A new career management simulator for golf fans
lede: Rainy Day Golf Pro brings the depth of classic sports management sims to the digital green. Players manage equipment, skill progression, and multi-season tournament circuits in a browser-based RPG format.

headline: DuckDB 2.0 adopts client-server architecture
lede: Codenamed Cyanoptera, the new release introduces native protocol support and a redesigned SQL parser. These advancements solidify the database's role in long-running, multi-tenant production environments.
